title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC1RE_0LE0LD_1LC0LB_0RA0RF_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC1RE_0LE0LD_1LC0LB_0RA0RF_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. It writes a word of blocks 1100 and 10 that grows to the right logarithmically slowly, like a counter. This page lists what has been established.
verdict: The question is open. Only first-look facts are established: no halt in 2·1010 steps, logarithmic growth, and the local pattern that halting needs.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 299 cells have been visited and 155 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is F on 1, and F is entered only from E on 1 (0RF): the machine halts exactly when E reads a 1 followed by another 1, E>1 1.

claims.title: Logarithmic growth
claims.text: The tape grows mostly to the right; the time to reach a new rightmost cell grows by a roughly constant factor per cell (cell 50 at step 1,089, cell 350 at step 16,667,114,039); 359 cells after 18,417,187,404 steps, no halt.

claims.title: What the tape is
claims.text: Read as words a = 1100 and b = 10 (tools/c/tokrun.c), the tape is a string over a, b and single 1s, a counter-like word whose front changes at every pass and whose back is a long regular tail (1 b^2)^n that grows by one unit now and then. The sibling 1RB0RD_1LC1RE_1LD0LC_0LE0LC_0RA0RF_1RA--- (C and D swapped, two transitions differ) behaves the same way.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. This machine grows a word of 1100 and 10 blocks to the right, each new cell costing a constant factor more time.

sections.heading: A word that grows slowly to the right
html: The machine grows its tape mostly to the right, each new cell costing a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter. Rightmost cell reached and the step it was first reached (direct run of 2·1010 steps):

Read in the words a = 1100 and b = 10, the tape is a word like a^6 b^14 a 1 b^2 a^3 1 b^4 a^5 … followed by a regular tail (1 b^2)^n. Its front changes at every pass of the head; the rule is not yet known.

sections.heading: What halting would take
html: The only halting transition is F on 1, and F is entered only from E on 1 (0RF): the machine halts exactly when E reads a 1 followed by another 1, E>1 1. It has not happened in 2·1010 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.063).
After 109 steps the tape spans 299 cells (31 left of the start, 262 right), with a density of 1s of 0.518.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Grows a word of 1100 / 10 blocks slowly to the right (one cell per constant factor of time), like a counter; halting needs E>1 1; sibling of 1RB0RD_1LC1RE_1LD0LC_0LE0LC_0RA0RF_1RA---.
